title: Everything through Tor
description: Every connection of the sandbox, the agent's own API connections included, leaves through Tor; lookups go to Tor's resolver and .onion names work. The allow-list, approvals and the connection proxy apply as always.

tor.label: Tor profile (sandbox-ai vpn list)
tor.hint: once: sandbox-ai build tor; sandbox-ai vpn add anon --tor --socks (--bridges FILE for obfs4 bridges, --exit-country CC)

notes: Make the profile once: sandbox-ai build tor, then sandbox-ai vpn add anon --tor --socks (--bridges FILE for obfs4 bridges, --exit-country de); sandbox-ai vpn check anon tries it alone. The value must name a Tor profile (another type of VPN profile is refused).
Before the agent starts tor must bootstrap, check.torproject.org must see a Tor exit, and tor's resolver must answer and map an .onion name; a failed check stops the start.
TCP over IPv4 only: no UDP (no QUIC, ping or NTP) and no IPv6; slower than without, and many sites, the agent's provider among them, may refuse or challenge Tor exits.
.onion names resolve into 10.192.0.0/10 and connect through Tor; with --dns (set here) every .onion the agent looks up, not only those of its allow-list.

With --socks in the profile, 127.0.0.1:9050 in the sandbox is Tor's SocksPort for programs that speak SOCKS (curl --socks5-hostname, torsocks, Tor Browser with TOR_SKIP_LAUNCH=1); what goes through it passes the connection proxy by. torsocks and Tor Browser in the agent's image: sandbox-ai images recipe tor --from AGENT, sandbox-ai build tor, then add --image-variant tor.
The exit relay sees what is not encrypted: use HTTPS. Podman only (the tunnel runs in a container of the pod).
